newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian Explorers Index falls 0.96 pct.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Explorers Index falls 0.96 pct.

text.p: Stockbroker Eyres Reed Ltd said its Australian Explorers Index fell 27 points or 0.96 percent last week. The All Ordinaries index fell 0.69 percent.
Sept 13 Sept 6 pct 1 Month pct 1 Year pct
NOTE: The explorers index (base 500, March 1992) tracks the performance of 88 small capitalisation exploration companies.
The Eyres Reed Explorer Index fell 27 points this week amid good volumes.
"While most of the blue suits in the east worried about BHP, there were plenty focussed on the relaunch of Joe Gutnick's diamond outfit, Astro Mining," Eyres Reed said.

"Astro's 20 cent shares went back into orbit at A$4.00, although most of the interest was purely awe and amazement rather than personal gain, because of the extremely restricted spread of the shares," it said.
"Joe Gutnick's record with the share prices of Great Central, Centaur, Astro and others has bought the entreprenuer back in to fashion this week."

Eyres Reed said Mark Savage's public company return saw the price of Growth Resources rise 15.7 cents to 22 cents. Tanganyika Gold rose to 27.5 cents from 23 cents while Australilan Kimberley Diamonds announced some bulk sampling results from the Blina Alluvial prospect and firmed from eight cents to 10.5 cents.
Diamin Resources rose to 7.1 cents from 5.7 at the beginning of the week as news filtered through from drilling into suspected kimberlite at Mad Gap Yard.
Ballarat Consolidated fell to seven cents from 10 cents and Golden Tiger fell again to 80 cents from A$1.00.
